# Evaluation of Skew-Reduction Options

## Option 1: Rebuild the static owner map against expected activation cost — **Dead on arrival**

**Why:** The profile already shows 86% of the skew is an *order statistic* — the `max` over 64 ranks of a stochastic per-step load. Rebalancing the *mean* load per rank does not change the variance of the per-step maximum. If each rank's load is roughly i.i.d. with the same distribution, the expected maximum of N samples grows as `O(√(log N))` relative to the mean. You can make every rank's *average* activation cost identical and the `max-over-ranks` span will still be dominated by whichever rank got unlucky on a given step. This is a fundamental property of barrier-synchronised parallelism with stochastic workloads; no static assignment can fix it.
